problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in degrees, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions to the equation  $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-0.4,$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$   are

$x≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$, $\,x≈$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-0.4)=-23.578\,178{…}^{∘}≈-{23.578}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $x=-{23.578}^{∘}$ is not in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ To get the first solution that's within the required domain, we need to find an angle that's coterminal with $-{23.578}^{∘}.$ To do this, we simply add ${360}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{23.578}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}={336.422}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Our first solution lies in the fourth quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={23.578}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={23.578}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951962/assets/c587e119531c3363816f72e9f2e1acdcc1aba87f278caa658342cbff144b0dad.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{23.578}^{∘} \\  & ={203.578}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions are 

$$
x≈{204}^{∘},\,x≈{336}^{∘}.
$$
